catalog_scope: Case-local governed knowledge assets; not a Platform Core registry and not callable implementations
source_read_boundary: All records were formed from the pinned source before this catalog was frozen. Rediscovery must use this file only.

assets.problem_solved: Avoid paying the cost and bias of querying long-term memory on every Agent turn.
assets.mechanism_summary: A small-model gate receives the current message, returns a narrow retrieve/skip decision plus a search query and reason, and the memory facade searches semantic and episodic stores only when the decision is retrieve. Parsing failure or gate failure fails open to retrieval with the original message as query.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns the pre-retrieval decision and query handoff. It does not own the memory stores, ranking, prompt assembly, or durable writes.
assets.state_semantics: Reads no durable state itself and writes no durable state. The decision is ephemeral per turn; downstream stores are read only on retrieve.
dependencies: model-provider client using the Waku message shape
assets.replaceability: Replaceable if the replacement preserves an explicit decision/query/reason contract, bounded cost, and fail-open semantics.
reuse_preconditions: A case-specific retrieval policy and relevant store/query contract exist
a cheap decision path is available or a deterministic substitute is authorized
fail-open behavior and false-positive retrieval cost are governed
gate decisions are recorded for later review
known_limits: Model decisions are not deterministic quality proof
a fail-open outage retrieves rather than skipping
the prompt encodes personal-assistant assumptions
the mechanism does not solve ranking or memory correctness
Waku_specific_assumptions: The query is for one user's facts, plans, preferences, and past events
semantic and episodic stores expose search methods
the active small model is configured by Waku settings

source_evidence.finding: One narrow JSON decision with query/reason; parse and API failures fail open.
Gate event is emitted and both semantic and episodic stores are queried only after retrieve.
Gated retrieval is part of working-memory assembly.
Decision, query propagation, single-call shape, and fail-open behavior are pinned offline.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: Do not reconstruct or execute in Case 02-A. If authorized later, first define the case's retrieval policy, store interface, decision audit fields, and failure budget; keep the gate external to Platform Core unless a separate platform authorization exists.

assets.problem_solved: Turn a model tool request into a bounded multi-step Agent action without allowing an unending loop.
assets.mechanism_summary: Each iteration sends the current working messages and tool schemas to the model, appends the assistant response, executes every requested tool, emits tool events, appends tool results as new working context, and repeats until no tool call is returned or max_iterations is reached. The hard-stop reply is explicit.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns turn-level reason/act/observe control, iteration counting, tool-result feedback, natural termination, and hard termination. It does not own gateway transport, memory policy, provider wire conversion, or durable persistence.
assets.state_semantics: Working messages are ephemeral per turn and are mutated in place. The resulting reply/tool summary is later persisted by the application/session layer; the loop itself does not write durable state.
assets.replaceability: Highly replaceable as a responsibility, provided the replacement preserves tool-call correlation, result feedback, observable iteration count, natural completion, and a hard termination bound.
reuse_preconditions: A governed model/tool message contract exists
tool calls have identity and bounded execution semantics
max iteration and max token policies are chosen per case
the hard-stop outcome is distinguishable from a successful natural reply
known_limits: Model may request ineffective or repeated tools
tools can have side effects before the hard stop
the loop does not independently validate tool arguments or semantic answer quality
live model behavior is not verified without a credential
Waku_specific_assumptions: Tool results are strings acceptable to the model
the client exposes Anthropic Messages-shaped content blocks
the assistant persona tells the model not to repeat a tool within a request

source_evidence.finding: The complete reason/act/observe loop and both exit conditions are implemented in one function.
The application assembles working memory and delegates the actual turn to the loop.
Natural one-iteration completion and hard-stop behavior are tested without a live model.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: Do not make this a Catalyst Runtime or generic Workflow standard in this stage. A later bounded proof would need explicit identity, cancellation, side-effect, timeout, and provenance policy before any reconstruction.

assets.asset_name: Observer fan-out with append-only turn trace
assets.problem_solved: Let gateways display live Agent events while the same events are persisted as inspectable turn evidence and optional telemetry spans.
assets.mechanism_summary: The application composes gateway, tracer, and capture observers. The tracer writes UTF-8 JSONL turn_start, gate, llm, tool, graph, and turn_end events, appends token usage to a separate ledger, and optionally maps events to OpenTelemetry spans. Streaming text is kept for the live observer and excluded from the durable trace.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns event fan-out and operational evidence recording. It does not decide Agent behavior, own business state, or provide a provenance identity model for an external platform.
assets.state_semantics: Writes append-only trace and usage files under WAKU_HOME; trace encoding is checked before append and legacy non-UTF-8 files are refused without modification.
assets.replaceability: Replaceable by an event sink or provenance recorder, but event identity, ordering, encoding, redaction, and failure policy must be specified first.
reuse_preconditions: A stable event vocabulary and run identity are defined
append/write failure behavior is governed
sensitive prompts/tool arguments are redacted or explicitly permitted
downstream consumers can tolerate missing live text events
known_limits: Current JSONL is local evidence, not tamper-proof provenance
events can include user messages and tool outputs
usage records use current provider/model settings and do not prove billing
OTel is optional and not live-verified here
Waku_specific_assumptions: one local process can append the daily file
dashboard reads the Waku event shape

source_evidence.finding: Fan-out, JSONL trace lifecycle, usage ledger, UTF-8 safety, and optional OTel are implemented.
Gateway observation and tracer persistence share the same event path.
Encoding and non-modification behavior are pinned offline.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: Treat as a candidate evidence/provenance seam, not as a drop-in Catalyst tracing standard. A later proof must bind external-agent identity, source commit, run/correlation id, actor attribution, redaction, and retention policy.

assets.asset_name: Separated deterministic completion, model quality judge, and release gate
assets.problem_solved: Make release decisions distinguish observable task completion from open-ended response quality, while allowing missing judge credentials to remain explicit.
assets.mechanism_summary: Deterministic scoring checks expected tool calls, arguments, and minimum call counts. A separate judge scores reply quality on a bounded rubric and degrades to no score on judge failure. The release gate requires deterministic success, runs judge evaluation only when the active provider has a key, records reports/history, and labels no-key judge evaluation as skipped.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns evaluation-axis separation and release decision composition. It does not own the Agent loop, model selection, or deployment authorization.
assets.state_semantics: Reads static eval datasets and writes eval_report.json plus append-only eval_runs.jsonl under the configured Waku home when the release gate runs.
assets.replaceability: Replaceable as a case-local release policy; the two-axis distinction and explicit skipped/not-live status should survive any implementation change.
reuse_preconditions: Observable completion criteria can be written without a model judge
quality rubric and threshold are case-specific
judge identity is independent or explicitly governed
missing credentials are a declared evidence state rather than a structural failure
known_limits: A judge score is model-based and not deterministic truth
the default release gate does not prove production safety
the judge can be unavailable or return unparseable output
the source's live eval behavior is not verified in this run
Waku_specific_assumptions: Tool-call records are the completion ground truth
DeepEval/pytest suites exist at the repository paths
Waku home is writable for reports

source_evidence.finding: Completion is deterministic over expected tool and argument outcomes.
Quality is a separate bounded model-based score with parse and availability degradation.
Deterministic pass gates release; judge runs only with an active key, otherwise status is skipped and reported.
Offline tests pin judge failure degradation.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: Do not turn this into a generic Platform release gate in Case 02-A. If reused later, map deterministic checks, judge rubric, threshold, evaluator identity, artifact retention, and authorization owner to the selected Catalyst case.

assets.asset_name: Bounded wave graph with code-owned routing and disjoint state writes
assets.problem_solved: Represent known parallel and conditional work around an Agent loop while keeping execution bounded, traceable, and testable.
assets.mechanism_summary: Graph nodes return state keys, independent ready nodes run in a wave, writes are merged in deterministic wave order, parallel key collisions raise, routers are plain code over state, and max_visits plus max_steps bound cycles. A full Agent loop can be used as one node; graph workflows therefore arrange the loop rather than replacing it.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns graph scheduling, dependency barriers, routing, state merge collision detection, node error capture, and graph-level bounds. It does not own the model's internal reasoning or tool semantics.
assets.state_semantics: One in-memory dict is the graph blackboard; node outputs merge into it, underscore-prefixed plumbing keys are excluded, and graph errors remain in state[errors]. No durable state is owned by the engine.
assets.replaceability: Replaceable for workflows whose shape is known ahead of time; not a replacement for open-ended Agent loops or a general workflow standard.
reuse_preconditions: The work shape is known and parallel branches can declare disjoint outputs
routing is code-governed and testable
global and per-node termination limits are explicit
node side effects and failure recovery are authorized
known_limits: A graph can encode the wrong shape for exploratory work
parallelism does not make external side effects transactional
state collision is detected after node execution
workflow semantics remain domain-specific
Waku_specific_assumptions: Waku's triage/gather nodes use ordinary Python callables
full_agent may call the Waku loop as a node

source_evidence.finding: Wave execution, state merge, code routers, bounds, errors, and topology description are explicit.
The optional front door runs classifier and calendar in parallel, then routes quick or full; the full path reuses the loop.
Known independent scans fan in to synthesis and a code router; the workflow is proposal-only.
Parallelism, collision protection, routing, and hard bounds are pinned offline.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: No graph adapter or Catalyst workflow change is authorized. A later case-local proof must first decide whether the need is predetermined structure or open-ended agentic work, then govern state ownership and side effects.

assets.problem_solved: Make repeatable instructions available without loading every instruction body into every Agent turn.
assets.mechanism_summary: SkillLoader scans inexpensive SKILL.md frontmatter and descriptions, matches by transparent keyword overlap, and loads only the bodies of the top matching skills into the prompt. It rescans when skill files change and supports bundled plus home-local skill directories.
assets.responsibility_boundary: Owns procedural instruction discovery and prompt inclusion. It does not decide semantic/episodic memory retrieval, execute tools, or certify the safety of an installed instruction.
assets.state_semantics: Reads skill files and keeps an in-memory parsed list/signature; it may load or refresh changed instructions, but does not write durable memory itself.
assets.replaceability: Replaceable with another governed instruction-discovery strategy; the progressive-disclosure boundary is the reusable idea, not the keyword matcher itself.
reuse_preconditions: Instructions have trusted metadata and an explicit body-loading boundary
installed content is reviewed before being eligible
matching misses and collisions are observable
prompt budget and maximum inclusions are bounded
known_limits: Keyword overlap misses synonyms and non-Latin terms
matching does not prove instruction safety or correctness
file changes are detected by mtime signature
the installer can fetch remote content and is outside this stage's live verification
Waku_specific_assumptions: Procedural memory is represented as SKILL.md
the current user message is the only match query
a matched skill body is safe to place in the system prompt

source_evidence.finding: Metadata is scanned first, bodies are included only after keyword match, and changed files trigger refresh.
Bundled and WAKU_HOME skills are exposed through a small facade.
Only matching skill instructions are added to working prompt context.

assets.Catalyst_reconstruction_notes: Keep this as a knowledge candidate, not a generic Skill/Memory standard. Any later reuse requires instruction trust, provenance, review, and injection resistance policy.
